document_title: Fire & Gas Detection Layout - Preliminary Design Report

sections.title: 1. Scope and basis of design
sections.text: This report describes a preliminary fire and gas (F&G) detector layout for a {plant_name}. The layout was produced automatically from the plot plan by DetectorPlace and is intended as a starting point for review by a competent F&G engineer. It covers {n_fire_points} m² of graded fire hazard area and {n_gas_points} m² of credible gas release zones around {n_leaks} leak sources.

sections.title: 2. Method
sections.text: Equipment footprints, elevation bands, hazard grades and leak sources were extracted from the plot-plan drawing by computer vision (equipment IoU {vision_iou}% against the source geometry). {n_candidates} candidate flame detector configurations (position, mounting height and orientation) and {n_gas_candidates} gas detector positions were evaluated by 3D line-of-sight ray marching ({rays} detector-to-point checks). A multi-objective genetic algorithm (NSGA-II with repair and redundancy pruning) traded installed cost against risk-weighted coverage shortfall. The cheapest layout meeting every target was selected.

sections.title: 3. Performance targets and achieved coverage
sections.text: Targets follow the performance-based structure of ISA-TR84.00.07: a minimum coverage fraction per hazard grade, with voted (2ooN) coverage required in Grade A areas to support executive action. Target values are project assumptions and must be confirmed against the site F&G philosophy.

sections.title: 4. Detector schedule
sections.text: {n_flame} flame detectors and {n_gas} point gas detectors are proposed. Coordinates are in metres from the plot-plan origin (top-left); azimuth is measured clockwise from plant east on the drawing.

sections.title: 8. Cost estimate (Class 4, indicative)
sections.text: Rates are placeholders and must be replaced with current supplier quotations and company estimating norms before use.

sections.title: 9. Limitations and verification
sections.text: Geometric mapping assumes a 2.5D plant (equipment as extruded footprints), a fixed design fire height and an idealised detector cone with off-axis range loss. It does not model congestion below pipe racks, smoke obscuration, gas dispersion (CFD) or detector-specific polar diagrams. Results were re-checked against the source geometry ({truth_check}). This layout is advisory. It must be verified and signed off by a competent person before construction.
